findings.reason: a done-when that re-registers the expectation to whatever the code emits dissolves the guard the section exists to hold.
findings.text: §11's three done-when clauses cannot distinguish a correct result from any result: clause (1) only records three numbers, clause (2) restates a fact its own comment records as already landed ("the three-change causal account ... accepted by the lead", comment c-partial-r-20261116T235243862922), and clause (3) defines the new expected value as "the value the benchmark entry point measures there", so any implementation of the head satisfies it — and no clause names a negative control

findings.reason: a dispatched node reading the body would re-measure a fifteen-revision causal investigation the plan already records as complete, instead of doing the one remaining step.
findings.text: §11's body says "Nothing re-registers the value until the change is known" and lists "the corpus input, the frame's time slice, the conductor currents" as live candidates, while done-when (2) and the plan's own comment record the cause as settled and the cited record states "The physical input did not change" and that the full historical replay restores the registration to 1.321e-7

findings.reason: the coordinator composing the brief must invent the durable location, and a record written anywhere else is what the review's evidence-path check exists to catch.
findings.text: §11 sends the benchmark's output to "this node's evidence directory" and never names the fragment or receipt path, where §7 names its fragment and figures directory, §9 names its fragment, §12 its record and figures, and §13 its record and figures

findings.reason: the section is landed and no node will implement it, so the stale tense costs a reader's comprehension but changes no work.
findings.text: §10 is marked done yet its body states in the present tense that the builder "takes its plasma coupling rows from two kernels" and that "the `_moment_couplings` docstring claims all three rows are moments of one kernel; they are not", while at this revision the builder takes every plasma row from `build_flux_blocks` alone and the docstring states the single-kernel fact correctly
